text: One powerful example of this can be seen in well-researched primary and secondary coping strategies. People using primary coping try to directly alter the external environment through action or behavior modification to reduce stress. People in independent cultures are more likely to use primary coping [ 24 ]. In contrast, people using secondary coping try to alter either themselves or their appraisal of the situation. Secondary coping is more common in interdependent cultures [ 25 ].
source_label: Crossing the rice-wheat border: Not all intra-cultural adaptation is equal
